skill.name: quality-reviewer
skill.description: Reviews DevPrep AI TypeScript code with shell checks and detailed standards for size, complexity, imports, naming, architecture, ESLint, and type safety.
skill.summary: Runs project-specific quality checks and explains how to fix TypeScript and architecture violations.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: All 106 static alerts are false positives caused by documentation syntax, educational examples, or fixed local quality-check commands. The scripts inspect the declared frontend tree and run hardcoded linting commands without user-controlled command construction, and no prompt injection or exfiltration intent was found.

content.value_statement: Manual checks miss project-specific TypeScript and architecture violations. This skill runs focused scripts and explains fixes using DevPrep AI standards.
actual_capabilities: Counts non-comment TypeScript and TSX lines and flags files above 180 lines.
Runs ESLint with a cyclomatic complexity limit of 15.
Finds imports that traverse upward through two or more directories.
Validates top-level frontend source folders against the configured architecture.
Searches for lowercase interface declarations that violate the configured naming convention.
Runs file, complexity, import, architecture, naming, ESLint, and TypeScript checks together.
limitations: The checks assume a DevPrep AI project with frontend/src and six configured source folders.
The scripts require Bash, npm, npx, ESLint, and project type-check commands.
The naming script may miss PascalCase interfaces that lack the required I prefix.
Educational examples disable TypeScript and ESLint checks and are not production-ready components.

use_cases.title: Check Changes Before Commit
use_cases.description: Run the complete review and fix TypeScript, import, size, or complexity failures before committing.

use_cases.title: Enforce Project Architecture
use_cases.description: Identify source files and folders that violate the DevPrep AI six-folder structure.

use_cases.title: Add a CI Quality Gate
use_cases.description: Use the full-review exit status to stop builds when configured quality checks fail.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current DevPrep AI project. Run the full quality check and summarize each failure by file.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Quality Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the project for file size, complexity, imports, and naming. Explain each violation and suggest the smallest compliant fix.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Architecture and Imports
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the architecture and import checks. Group violations by module and propose path aliases or folder moves without changing behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Complete Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform the full review, prioritize failures by impact, and create a staged refactoring plan. Preserve behavior and identify checks to rerun after each stage.

output: File size and naming checks passed.
Two deep relative imports require configured aliases.
One function exceeds the complexity limit of 15.
ESLint and TypeScript results follow the custom checks.

output_examples.input: Explain how to fix an oversized form component.
output_examples.output: Split presentation, state logic, types, and optional utilities into focused files. Rerun size, complexity, lint, and type checks afterward.

output_examples.input: Check whether the source layout follows project standards.
output_examples.output: The review compares frontend/src folders with the configured architecture and reports files placed directly under src or in unsupported top-level folders.

best_practices: Run focused checks during development and the full review before merging.
Confirm each reported violation against project context before refactoring.
Rerun ESLint and TypeScript checks after moving files or changing imports.
anti_patterns: Do not apply the six-folder rules to unrelated project structures without adapting the scripts.
Do not treat educational examples with disabled checks as production templates.
Do not split files only to meet line limits when the result weakens clear module boundaries.

faq.question: Which projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It targets DevPrep AI TypeScript projects with frontend/src and the documented folder structure.

faq.question: Does the skill modify source files?
faq.answer: The bundled scripts report violations and return exit codes. Refactoring changes require a separate explicit request.

faq.question: What tools must be installed?
faq.answer: Bash, npm, npx, ESLint, and the project TypeScript checker must be available.

faq.question: Can it run in continuous integration?
faq.answer: Yes. The full-review script returns a failing exit status when any configured check fails.

faq.question: Why are deep relative imports rejected?
faq.answer: The project standard requires configured aliases for imports that move upward through two or more directories.

faq.question: Does it review security vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on code quality, TypeScript, imports, naming, complexity, and project architecture.
